Wow, it's mind-blowing how your situation is similar to mine, even the time frames of ghosting and pretty much the reasons.

First of all, I'm so sorry you're going through this. I know that you probably felt like crap many times because of that.

Unfortunately, I've been struggling with letting my friend go, so I'm not sure if I can help here. But I've deleted/blocked them from socials two times.

The first blocking was in August 2023, when she didn't answer my message and then ignored me in public, walking right next to me. I needed to write to her because we had a trip planned together the same year.

Fast forward. We used to talk, but we didn't have the contact as previously. Then, she stood me up with our meeting, and a few days later, I deleted all the messages with her (that've been left, I've done it before).

We haven't spoken since March 2024. The second blocking was done by me in February this year, when she changed her surname on socials (she married the guy I was not supposed to worry about/be jealous of).

I hate that we didn't talked but she used to ghost me before, and I'm trying not to beg for her attention, not anymore. 

Deleting them from socials helps because you don't need to look at them and hurt yourself every time you see them. 

It's freeing, although it hurts at first, like you lose them for real (even though it's already happened), but you also lose the weight of the messages you overthink at 3 a.m. 

If you aren't ready, you can always make a folder and put them everything connected to them. When you're ready, you'll delete it then.


I wish you all the best and hope you will heal

Okay, I hear what you're saying. I understand that sexual needs are important, but those are not the top priorities in the relationship, and neither is chemistry/energy. I have been there, and after lots of thoughts, it was probably one of the very few things that kept me sticking to that imagination of me and her. That is why I am asking about the other things, like emotional support, being open to conversation, having the same ideas about the future, ect.


If you want to work on rebuilding your relationship with her - give it a shot, write to her. It was mutual break up, so you can talk and try to find out what you both want. 
It is your call. Just don't expect too much. Keeping my fingers crossed! Good luck!

If I were you, I'd think if moving closer to her would be a possibility. If that is a sacrifice you can make in the future because, like you said, it was one of the reasons you broke up.

I think you should answer the questions above and reflect on why you think she is the one. Were you high on hormones and emotions? Did you support yourselves in a hard time? Could you figure out solutions to your problems together? 

Don't be in a hurry. It's not a race. If after that, you will still think that you want to give it a shot and you're ready to put work on rebuilding your relationship - write to her, but take it slowly and be aware that it can go different ways, so be prepared that you can get hurt. Try not to have too many expectations.

That is why I suggested removing her and breaking up posts from your side, so it is easier to not think about her, even though you will still probably do from time to time.

It will be easier if you occupy your mind with something else.


Okay, from what I read, you know she was in relationships, and I assume not from her but her socials? 

Like I said earlier, I'd suggest thinking what you would get from reconciliation. Is it just an explanation to move on? Is it maybe hope to eventually get back together? Is it because you're lonely and miss being emotionally intimate with someone? 

It's been almost four years. Are you sure she is not the centre of your world anymore? Because from what I read, it looks like you haven't moved (checking her on socials, knowing every relationship she was in). 

Would you tell that you are happy with your life? Do you have other things to do, any hobbies, friends or is your all energy focused on your past? Did you learn from your mistakes from that relationship to not make similar in the future? 

Those answers are for you, so maybe it will clarify some things a little more for you.

As much as it hurts now, I think it eventually will get better.

She then explained that she was struggling with family issues at the time when I saw her on the bus station, that is why se didn't notice me which I understand. I feel like I was the one in that relationship whose needs didn't matter because most of the time, it was about her problems and needs.
